title: BASALT local durability and remote authority engine qualification
claim_ceiling: Versioned candidate matrix and adversarial test plan only. No engine has been independently qualified by this suite.

arms.topology: single-host local file; one or more processes on same host

arms.client: Rust Turso binding pinned to exact release/commit (initial candidate 0.8.0)
arms.topology: in-process local file; multi-connection; no multi-process assumption
arms.durability_profile: WAL-compatible mode; PRAGMA synchronous=FULL; explicit checkpoint policy

arms.topology: PostgreSQL 18 server on same host; local client
PostgreSQL 18 primary over pinned regional network; no synchronous standby
arms.durability_profile: fsync=on; synchronous_commit=on; full_page_writes=on; primary-only authoritative reads

arms.topology: PostgreSQL 18 primary plus explicitly provisioned synchronous standbys
arms.durability_profile: fsync=on; synchronous_commit=on or remote_flush; synchronous_standby_names pinned; failover policy recorded

arms.topology: three-member cluster across declared failure domains
arms.durability_profile: linearizable reads; atomic scoped compare-and-advance; quorum commit

arms.topology: five-member cluster across declared failure domains
arms.durability_profile: linearizable reads; atomic scoped compare-and-advance; quorum commit
ACID transactions; reference KV control only; no relational parity claim

scenarios.mutation: Fresh local database; first small transaction on first connection; acknowledge COMMIT; power-loss model immediately afterward
New connection to an existing local database; first small non-spilling transaction; acknowledge COMMIT; power-loss model immediately afterward
Commit immediately after WAL checkpoint/truncate or WAL-generation reset
Large/spilling transaction whose pages are appended through alternate WAL paths
Several commits on one connection followed by power loss immediately after an acknowledged commit
Crash occurs while the sync call is in flight or returns an I/O error
Distinguish process SIGKILL from OS/power loss using the same acknowledged-commit protocol
Short write, disk full, fsync failure, or storage device I/O error during the four-record transition
Inject process crash/failure after each individual receipt/source/log/policy write before transaction commit
Crash after durable commit but before client receives the response
Retry receipt A after receipt B and unrelated state changes have advanced the current store revision
Two writers from the same source/generation and predecessor submit different receipt digests
Two independent source lineages with independent log origins advance from a common snapshot
Two distinct sources contend on one shared log checkpoint cursor
Policy or witness pointer changes after proof verification but before CAS/commit
Serializable PostgreSQL transaction fails with SQLSTATE 40001; retry only the final statement as an intentionally bad control
PostgreSQL SERIALIZABLE transaction fails with SQLSTATE 40001; retry the whole transaction including logic derived from reads
Supply stale replica, member-local serializable etcd read, or cache read as authority freshness evidence
Restore SQLite, Turso or PostgreSQL from an internally consistent older backup while keeping an old trusted authority identity
PostgreSQL point-in-time recovery creates a new timeline from an older target; external witness records the latest accepted-state commitment
Restore etcd snapshot without revision bump or mark-compacted
Restore etcd snapshot with --bump-revision and --mark-compacted
Restore a valid database snapshot but change authority incarnation identity or omit externally witnessed predecessor commitment
Witness/monitor is unavailable or disagrees with restored authority state
Delete local SQLite/Turso cache and rebuild it exclusively from remote immutable accepted receipt records
Fail over PostgreSQL with synchronous standbys and verify commit acknowledgment policy and promoted node history
Run the same four-record state transition and receipt bytes on every relational/coordination arm
redb handles the same narrow key/value data but is not compared on joins or relational query capabilities
